more_info.overview: Paprika oleoresin is used as a color in food. Its technological role is to add or restore food colour.
more_info.uses: EU permissions include ripened cheese, processed cheese, cheese products (excluding products falling in category 16), dried fruit and vegetables. These permissions depend on the food category and its conditions of use.
more_info.origin: Extracted from paprika fruit using permitted solvents, which are then removed. Capsanthin and capsorubin are the main colouring compounds.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The specified starting material is plant derived and compatible with vegetarian and vegan diets. The specification does not establish halal or kosher certification.
more_info.daily_intake: 24 mg paprika extract/kg body weight/day, equivalent to 1.7 mg carotenoids/kg body weight/day for the assessed extract (EFSA, 2015).
more_info.side_effects:
Refined food-use estimates were below EFSA's limit.
Animal studies found no cancer effect at the tested doses; tissue findings at higher exposure supported the intake limit.
